protocol.name: qdwin_locker_v1
protocol.description:
Private protocol between the qdwin compositor and the qdistro PyQt locker (qdlocker). Trust model: the bind handler always rejects clients whose peer uid does not match the admin-configured locker uid. In addition, when an expected locker executable path and/or SELinux label are configured (--qdwin-allowed-locker-exe= / QDWIN_ALLOWED_LOCKER_EXE and --qdwin-allowed-locker-label= / QDWIN_ALLOWED_LOCKER_LABEL), the handler resolves the peer's /proc/<pid>/exe and/or /proc/<pid>/attr/current and rejects the bind unless they match exactly. These checks fail closed: an unreadable or OOM /proc read is treated as "unverifiable" and rejects the bind, and the reads are bracketed by /proc/<pid>/stat starttime samples so a pid whose process identity is unstable across the read window is also rejected.
Residual window (be honest about scope): the peer pid is the value the kernel pinned at connect time, but /proc is read later when the bind request is handled, so the exe/label/starttime checks are best-effort defence-in-depth on top of the uid gate, not a proof that /proc still names the exact connecting process. The starttime double-read only proves the pid named one stable process across our own read window; it does not exclude (a) pid reuse that completed before the first sample, nor (b) a same-process execve() (e.g. into a different SELinux domain), because starttime is the fork/clone time and is unchanged by exec. The primary gate remains the uid check plus the socket being reachable only to the locker uid. When a check is left unconfigured it is skipped, and the compositor relies on systemd unit confinement and SELinux service policy to keep this socket reachable only to the locker process. The locker global is visible in the registry, but regular app clients cannot bind it because they run as a different uid (and, when configured, a different exe/label); the shell client (qdwin_shell_v1) cannot drive lock state through it either — the locker is a separate peer process from the shell.
Why a separate global from qdwin_shell_v1:
- The shell client and the locker client have different lifetimes. The shell can crash and restart while the locker is live; the locker can crash and restart while the shell is composing decorations. Wiring them through a single global would couple their lifecycles. - The real lock UI is the qdlocker Qt xdg_toplevel. qdwin promotes that toplevel to the LOCK layer by matching the already-authorized locker process identity, avoiding a fragile cross-display wl_surface handoff. - The locker is the only process allowed to drive the compositor's `locked` state. Keeping that authority on its own global lets qdwin filter it independently from the shell's chrome / focus requests.
The compositor remains authoritative over lock state. The locker requests `set_locked(1)`, but qdwin is the actor: it hides all non-lock surfaces, mutes input to them, and emits `locked_changed`. The shell observes via the existing qdwin_shell_v1 `locked_changed` event and swaps its UI off.
Warning! Experimental and pre-stable. Versioning follows the "experimental" convention: version 1 is the first unstable draft.

interface.name: qdwin_locker_v1
interface.description:
The locker binds this global once and holds it for the lifetime of its process. qdwin rejects a second bind from the same client. Only one locker may hold the role at a time. If a new `bind_as_locker` arrives while another locker is still bound, qdwin checks whether the current locker's peer process is still alive (its pid still names the same process by /proc starttime): if it is, the new bind is REFUSED with the `locker_present` error and the existing locker is left untouched. A takeover only succeeds once the prior locker's peer is proven dead (pid gone or recycled). This prevents a live same-uid duplicate from evicting the real locker and calling set_locked(0) to unlock the session.
Bootstrap: after `bind_as_locker`, qdwin accepts `set_locked(1)` immediately. If the Qt lock toplevel has not mapped yet, qdwin hides the normal desktop and shows a black screen until that toplevel appears, then promotes it to the LOCK layer.
If the locker process dies while the compositor is in locked state, qdwin keeps the screen black and refuses input until a replacement locker binds. Admin's compositor is the trusted computing base; a missing locker is fail-safe (locked), not fail-open.

entry.name: already_bound
entry.summary: bind_as_locker called twice on the same resource

entry.name: not_bound
entry.summary: request issued before bind_as_locker (or after the locker was torn down)

entry.name: locker_present
entry.summary: bind_as_locker refused because another locker is already bound and its peer process is still alive. Only one locker may hold the role at a time; a takeover is permitted only once the prior locker's peer is proven dead. A live duplicate must not be able to evict the real locker and call set_locked(0).

request.name: bind_as_locker
request.description: The locker announces that it is ready to receive lock-trigger events and to drive lock state. Must be the first request on the interface. qdwin replies with `ready` once it has confirmed the peer credentials and registered the binding.

event.name: ready
event.description: Sent after `bind_as_locker` succeeds. If the compositor is already locked, the locker should show its Qt lock window and wait for the user to authenticate.

arg.name: initially_locked
arg.summary: 1 if the compositor is currently locked, 0 otherwise

request.name: attach_lock_surface
request.description:
Legacy explicit lock-surface attach. Current qdlocker does not use this request; qdwin instead promotes qdlocker's real Qt xdg_toplevel to the compositor LOCK layer. This request is retained for compatibility with older lockers and tests.
The surface must not have a role yet. After attach, it has the implicit "lock surface" role; any wl_surface.commit triggers a frame on the LOCK layer.

request.name: set_locked
request.description:
`locked=1` → compositor enters the locked state: normal desktop layers are hidden, the lock layer remains visible, and input is delivered only to the locker via `overlay_key`. qdwin promotes the authorized locker's Qt toplevel to the lock layer when it maps. If it is not mapped yet, the screen stays black.
`locked=0` → unlocks; user surfaces resume rendering. The locker is expected to call this only after a successful authentication.
Compositor emits `locked_changed(locked)` to the shell on qdwin_shell_v1 after the transition completes, and emits the equivalent `locked_changed` event on this interface to the locker.
Older qdwin builds failed with `no_surface` if no explicit lock surface was attached. Current qdwin accepts the request and waits for the real locker toplevel.

event.name: locked_changed

description.summary: compositor entered or left locked state

event.description: Mirror of qdwin_shell_v1.locked_changed for the locker. Fires on every transition, including transitions the locker did not request (e.g. the compositor's fail-safe black screen when the bound locker process dies while locked).

event.name: lock_requested

description.summary: compositor relays a lock trigger to the locker

event.description:
The compositor relays a lock trigger to the locker. `reason` names which of the sessions.md §"Lock triggers" caused it:
reason = 0 idle — ext-idle-notify-v1 timeout reason = 1 lid — systemd-logind lid close reason = 2 suspend — prepare-for-sleep reason = 3 manual — Ctrl+Alt+L global hotkey or admin panel "Lock now"
Implementation note (current qdwin): the compositor only observes and emits `reason = 3` (the Ctrl+Alt+L hotkey). The locker sources the other triggers itself, NOT via this event: idle from its own idle timer, and lid/suspend by subscribing directly to systemd-logind (`Session.Lock` for lid, `PrepareForSleep` for suspend). Reasons 0/1/2 are reserved here so the wire format stays stable if a future qdwin observes them directly; today they are not sent.
The locker decides whether to call `set_locked(1)` (it usually does immediately, but may delay if a fingerprint verification is already in progress).

event.name: overlay_key
event.description:
While the compositor is locked, qdwin installs a keyboard grab and forwards each pressed key to the locker here. Identical wire format to qdwin_shell_v1.overlay_key (since v17) for the role=2 (locker) value, but delivered on the locker's connection so the shell cannot observe lock-time keystrokes — i.e. the password the user types never reaches the shell process.
`sym` is the xkb keysym; `utf8` is the printable character (or "" if non-printable). The locker prefers utf8 when non-empty and falls back to `sym` for control keys (Escape, Return, BackSpace, Tab).
Only PRESSED transitions are sent. Releases are absorbed by the grab.

request.name: lock_acknowledged
request.description: Tells the compositor the locker has handled (or deliberately ignored) a `lock_requested` event. Used for tests and for deciding whether the compositor should escalate (e.g. drop to a black screen if the locker fails to lock within a reasonable window after suspend).

arg.name: reason
arg.summary: must match the most recent lock_requested.reason

interface.name: qdwin_locker_surface_v1

description.summary: handle to a previously-attached lock surface

interface.description: Created by `qdwin_locker_v1.attach_lock_surface`. Destroying this object dismisses the lock surface; if the compositor is currently locked, the screen goes black until a fresh attach_lock_surface fires.

event.name: configure
event.description: Tells the locker the dimensions it should commit a buffer at to cover every output. Re-fires on output hot-plug or rotation.
